person.name: Gerald Fenwick-Starr
person.target_direction: Plant manager in another industry, or director of operations

roles.title: Plant Manager
roles.context: Single-site Tier 2 automotive supplier of injection-molded interior trim and under-hood components. 210 employees (186 hourly, United Steelworkers local), 3 shifts, 42 presses (85 to 1,100 ton). Plant P&L owner reporting to the COO: about $96M annual sales, $38M controllable operating budget. 7 direct reports (production, maintenance, quality, EHS, materials, engineering, HR generalist).

accomplishments.title: OEE improvement program
accomplishments.problem: Plant-wide OEE was 61% in 2018 with frequent unplanned press downtime and no consistent downtime tracking.
accomplishments.actions: Installed press-level downtime tracking linked to Plex MES, started tiered daily accountability meetings (cell, department, plant), launched TPM with operator autonomous maintenance checklists on the 12 highest-volume presses, and prioritized mold PM.
accomplishments.results: OEE rose from 61% (2018) to 78% (2024); unplanned downtime cut roughly in half. Avoided a planned $2.4M capital purchase of two additional presses because recovered capacity covered a new program launch.

accomplishments.title: Scrap reduction
accomplishments.problem: Scrap ran 4.8% of material cost, mostly short shots, splay, and flash on three high-volume part families.
accomplishments.actions: Ran Green Belt DMAIC projects with the quality and process engineers: scientific molding process windows, resin drying verification, and standard work for startups after mold changes.
accomplishments.results: Scrap fell from 4.8% to 2.1% of material cost, about $610K annual savings in resin and rework.

accomplishments.title: Safety turnaround
accomplishments.problem: TRIR was 4.2 in 2018 with repeated hand and ergonomic injuries; corporate flagged the site.
accomplishments.actions: Started daily safety Gemba walks, a near-miss reporting program with no-blame follow-up, light-curtain and guarding audits on all presses, and an ergonomics review of the 10 worst-rated jobs with the joint union-management safety committee.
accomplishments.results: TRIR dropped from 4.2 to 1.3 by 2023; plant reached 500 days without a lost-time injury in 2024.

accomplishments.title: IATF 16949 certification
accomplishments.problem: Major OEM customer required the plant to move from ISO 9001 to IATF 16949 by end of 2019 to stay on bid lists.
accomplishments.actions: Sponsored the transition: funded a quality systems coordinator, led management reviews, drove PFMEA and control plan updates for all active part numbers, and personally ran the layered process audit program.
accomplishments.results: Certified on first attempt in Nov 2019 with zero major nonconformances; plant remained eligible for two new programs worth about $14M in annual sales.

accomplishments.title: Union relations during contract renewal
accomplishments.problem: 2021 contract renewal came after a difficult prior negotiation and grievance backlog of 30+ open items.
accomplishments.actions: Held monthly labor-management meetings, worked the grievance backlog down before talks, and was a member of the company bargaining team.
accomplishments.results: Contract ratified without work stoppage; grievance backlog cleared. He describes the relationship as 'night and day' compared with 2018. No quantifiable outcome beyond that.

roles.title: Production Manager
roles.context: Thermoformed and printed food-service packaging (cups, lids, clamshells). Managed thermoforming and printing departments: 4 supervisors, about 95 hourly employees (Teamsters), 14 thermoforming lines and 3 printing presses.

accomplishments.title: SMED changeover reduction on thermoforming lines
accomplishments.problem: Tool changeovers on thermoformers were long and unpredictable, so scheduling ran long runs and built excess inventory.
accomplishments.actions: Led a SMED kaizen: moved tasks external, staged tooling carts, standardized clamps, and created changeover checklists; trained all 4 supervisors to run follow-on events.
accomplishments.results: He remembers changeovers going from about 90 minutes to about 25, with roughly 30 changeovers a week across the 14 lines. Finished-goods inventory dropped, but he does not know by how much.

accomplishments.title: Customer complaint reduction on printed cups
accomplishments.problem: A national quick-service restaurant customer issued a corrective action for print registration defects.
accomplishments.actions: Ran root cause analysis (5-why, fishbone) with the press crew, added first-piece inspection and hourly print checks with go/no-go standards.
accomplishments.results: Corrective action closed in 60 days and the customer did not re-source the business (about $8M per year account). No complaint-rate data retained.

accomplishments.title: Cross-training matrix for printing department
accomplishments.problem: Only 2 people per shift could run the 8-color press, causing overtime and missed shipments when they were absent.
accomplishments.actions: Built a skills matrix and cross-training plan; paired senior operators with trainees.
accomplishments.results: Qualified operators went from 6 to 15 across 3 shifts; department overtime fell from about 14% to 8% of hours.

roles.title: Production Supervisor, 2nd Shift
roles.context: Supervised about 30 hourly employees on 2nd shift across thermoforming.

accomplishments.title: 2nd shift attendance improvement
accomplishments.problem: 2nd shift had the worst attendance and the most missed production targets.
accomplishments.actions: Introduced shift-start huddles, posted hourly production boards, and applied the attendance policy consistently with the union steward.
accomplishments.results: Qualitative: shift went from last to first in plant attainment rankings within about a year; no records kept.

accomplishments.title: New hire training standard work
accomplishments.problem: New operators were trained inconsistently by whoever was available.
accomplishments.actions: Wrote job instruction sheets for 6 core thermoforming jobs using TWI Job Instruction method.

roles.title: Process Engineer
roles.context: Metal stamping and welded assemblies for appliance OEMs.

accomplishments.title: Weld cell fixture redesign
accomplishments.problem: A robotic weld cell had high rework from part misalignment.
accomplishments.actions: Redesigned fixture locating pins and clamps (AutoCAD), validated with a capability study in Minitab.
accomplishments.results: Weld rework on that cell dropped from about 6% to under 1%; Cpk on the critical dimension went from 0.9 to 1.5.

accomplishments.title: PFMEA facilitation
accomplishments.problem: PFMEAs were out of date for older part numbers.
accomplishments.actions: Facilitated PFMEA updates with cross-functional teams for 12 part families.
